newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan in bid to broker Afghan peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan in bid to broker Afghan peace talks.

text.p: Pakistan offered on Tuesday to arrange peace talks between warring factions in neighbouring Afghanistan as it sent a high-level delegation to sound out the parties on the proposal.

The delegation led by Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar met officials of the Taleban Islamic movement that took over Kabul last month, and also visited Mazar-i-Sharif, the base of the powerful warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum who controls six northern provinces.

"The delegation would be conveying the readiness of the government of Pakistan to bring the Afghan groups together to resolve their differences peacefully and agree on a broad-based arrangement that could bring durable peace to Afghanistan," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
It was not immediately clear whether Pakistan was planning to invite the parties to talks on its territory or would try to broker a dialogue inside Afghanistan.
"The visit is a continuation of (Pakistan's) efforts...to evolve a peaceful solution to the crisis in Afghanistan and ensure an end to the current fighting and loss of life," the statement said.
It said Islamabad had been maintaining contacts with Afghan groups to promote this objective and "the present visit has been undertaken to build on the groundwork that has already been done".
It was the highest-level delegation to visit Afghanistan since the Taleban took over the capital on September 27.
No countries have yet formally recognised the Taleban government, though Pakistan has said it would deal with the "new government" in Kabul.

Acting Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told a news conference in Kabul that the delegation "met with our authorities and they discussed some issues which normally two neighbouring countries should discuss".
The Taleban movement was formed in refugee camps in Pakistan two years ago, and according to its opponents has enjoyed logistical support from Islamabad.
Pakistan denies the charges, saying it has no favourites among the Afghan groups, most of which it helped during their guerrilla war against Soviet occupation in 1980s.
On the Pakistani delegation's plans to visit Mazar-i-Sharif for talks with Dostum, who signed a political agreement with other militia opposing the Taleban on Monday, Mutaqi said:
"We told them we don't have any problems with the forces in Mazar-i-Sharif and we are ready to solve the issues through negotiations and understanding with Mazar."
